Jess (support): Heads-up — BrightGrid (dedicated pool eu-west-1) reports intermittent 503s + auth failures since 09:20 UTC, plus big p90 token latency spikes. Customer sees failures on retries too.
Maya (eng): Thanks Jess. Any tenant ID or pool id? Are they on MIG partitioning or full GPUs?
Jess (support): Tenant ID bg-773, pool: dedicated-eu2-3, they asked for 1g. Partitioning: MIG 7g. They said behavior started after a customer autoscale yesterday.
BrightGrid Ops: Confirming logs — repeated: "token verification failed" while the same request later succeeds. Also p95 tokens go from 60ms to 2.1s.
Sanjay (infra): Probable noisy neighbor. Can you paste a small sample of the error/response headers? Also did billing spikes come with it?
Jess (support): Billing spike yes — audit shows sudden token usage burst + a couple of OVERRUN throttle events. Sample error (copied):
```
ERROR 2026-03-17T09:22:11Z request_id=abc123 status=503: upstream inference error
x-request-retry: 1
x-auth-status: transient_fail
```

Maya (eng): 503 + auth transient_fail on initial attempt smells like connection starvation on the model process or intermittent auth proxy timeouts. Can BrightGrid repro? If so, need seq of requests and exact header set.
BrightGrid Ops: We reproduced with a burst script: 50 concurrent requests, each 2k tokens. Repro steps:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"...2k tokens"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
```
We see ~6% 503s and some 401-like auth transient messages.
Maya (eng): Good repro. Can we check node-level metrics for that dedicated host? GPU utl, SM utilization, MIG slice mapping.
Sanjay (infra): Pulling metrics now — host node-rt-eu2-14 shows one MIG instance with at times 100% SM utilization and increased L3 cache misses. Several co-tenants on same physical host have small but overlapping burst windows.
Luca (oncall): Autoscale-bot shows the pool attempted to spin up another node but failed due to quota for region; fallback kept requests on saturated host.
autoscale-bot: action: attempted_scale_up pool=dedicated-eu2-3 reason=burst failed_quota=GPU-QUOTA-EU2
Maya (eng): That exactly explains it — no extra capacity, so shared host suffered thrash. MIG slices can still interfere via shared L3 and PCIe if neighbors are heavy.
Jess (support): Customer also reported auth proxy between edge and private control plane saw spikes in latency around same time — maybe retries overloaded the auth service.
Sanjay (infra): We saw short auth-proxy CPU escalations on the control plane floor. The retry storm from BrightGrid's burst likely amplified the auth latency, causing transient auth failures.
Maya (eng): Mitigation plan: 1) Throttle or limit concurrency for that tenant until we get more capacity. 2) Temporarily pin them to less crowded nodes (migrate off host-rt-eu2-14). 3) Investigate autoscale quota failure and request quota bump for eu-west-1. 4) Add short-term rate-limiter on auth-proxy to avoid cascading failures.
Jess (support): I've applied a conservative concurrency cap for bg-773 (20 concurrent) and scheduled a manual migration to a different node with lower colocated load. Notifying customer now.
BrightGrid Ops: Thanks — after we dropped concurrency we see errors disappear and p95 back to normal. Will need timeline for permanent fix.
Luca (oncall): Filing incident tracker: INC-2026-042. Need follow-ups: quota request, node migration audit, autoscale behavior replay, and auth-proxy resilience.
Maya (eng): Also recommend we add a metric for MIG neighbor noise: correlate p99 L3 misses + SM throttling with tenant error rates. Could help auto-detect noisy neighbors before customer impact.
Sanjay (infra): Agreed. I'll open infra task to add that signal and create a dashboard. Also will request quota bump and schedule capacity test.
Jess (support): Closing the customer-facing loop: told BrightGrid we'll keep cap for 24h while we migrate and request quota. They accepted.
BrightGrid Ops: Appreciate quick action. Please include migration ETA.
Maya (eng): ETA for safe migration: 2h to cold migrate with minimal impact (we'll drain existing inflight requests). If anything changes I will post updates here.
Jess (support): Noted. Thanks everyone.
Luca (oncall): Postmortem owner please? Maya / Sanjay?
Maya (eng): I'll own postmortem, Sanjay for infra follow-ups.
Sanjay (infra): Happy to.
Maya (eng): Follow-ups: add MIG-noise alert, quota request, auth-proxy rate limit, migration audit. I'll file JIRA after this thread.
Jess (support): Thread summary added to INC-2026-042. Closing slack thread once migration completes. :thumbsup:
